title: Revamp tracing and metrics pipeline for lower overhead and OTEL upgrade
creator: Tomas Rivera
description: Scope: Upgrade services of the inference runtime and console microservices to the newer OpenTelemetry stacks and clean up high-overhead metrics/logging paths. This ticket focuses on three pillars: 1) OTEL library upgrades and semantic-convention alignment, 2) tracing hook refactor to remove blocking behavior on hot paths, and 3) metrics logging changes to reduce cardinality and CPU impact. Goals: reduce telemetry overhead on tail latency, cut CPU usage from periodic runtime metrics collection, and consolidate exporters to OTLP/gRPC with non-blocking exporters and batching. Not in scope: changing core business metrics definitions or telemetry for 3rd-party integrations (follow-up tickets will cover those).
acceptance_criteria: All runtime services upgraded to OpenTelemetry components defined in the upgrade doc (collector-compatible OTLP/gRPC exporters)
No synchronous span exportors on request-critical code paths; batch span processor with async export configured and validated
Remove per-request runtime.ReadMemStats calls and replace with a single periodic sampler for all services (max 1% additional CPU in benchmarks)
Reduce top-cardinality metric labels for hot endpoints (no path-level label per request) and pass CI metric-regression checks
Automated smoke tests demonstrate <= 5% regression in p50 and <= 10% in p99 for standard synthetic workload; and CPU reduction on collector-less path for internal load tests
Rollout plan with canary + automatic rollback on telemetry regressions defined in runbook
updates: 2026-02-20 — Created ticket after infra spike showed collector CPU on prod-tier services rose ~12% during load testing; initial profiling pointed to synchronous span export and frequent memstats collections.

2026-02-25 — Spike: upgraded otel-go to 1.13 in a sandbox branch; replaced sync exporter with BatchSpanProcessor and non-blocking OTLP/gRPC exporter. Measured p99 tail improvement of ~10ms on small benchmark (see linked PR).

2026-03-01 — Decision: standardize on OTLP/gRPC + resource attributes in headers for tenant routing. Agreed to remove 'path' as a high-cardinality label for http_server_duration; instead tag with route_name where available.

2026-03-05 — Implemented centralized MetricsSampler (periodic 5s) to replace ad-hoc runtime.ReadMemStats calls sprinkled across services. Local microbench: CPU use for metrics dropped from 6.1% -> 2.8% under 500 req/s load.

2026-03-08 — Code review feedback: need explicit retry/backoff policy for exporter and a feature-flag gated rollout per service. Added feature flag `otel_pipeline_v2` and health checks to ensure exporter readiness.

2026-03-12 — Canary deployment started to 10% of traffic for runtime-gateway in eu-west. Observability dashboards show no increase in error-rate; exporter queue length stable. Next: broaden to 25% and run 24h soak.
linked_prs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4182 — otel: introduce batch span processor and OTLP exporter
https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/233 — metrics: replace per-request memstats with MetricsSampler
https://github.com/redwood-inference/common/pull/112 — tracing: unify hook API and add async flush helpers
risks: Exporter backpressure might cause queue growth if collector endpoint is misconfigured — mitigation: exporter queue size limit + health check triggers rollback
Cardinality mistakes during migration could spike TSDB costs — mitigation: preflight metric-validation job and metric-regression CI
Feature flag misconfiguration could leave some services with mixed OTEL semantic conventions — mitigation: integration test that asserts resource attributes and semantic names
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): 10% traffic, 24h soak, validate latency and exporter queue metrics
Phase 2: 25% traffic, 48h soak; run metric-regression job; expand to eu-west + us-central
Phase 3: 100% traffic, monitor 7 days, deprecate old exporters and remove legacy tracing wrappers
Rollback: toggling feature flag `otel_pipeline_v2` to false and POST /admin/telemetry/flush to force synchronous flush during rollback window
notes: Benchmarks used: local k6 scripts simulating 1000 concurrent sessions with realistic prefix caching patterns
Perf delta observed in sandbox: p99 latency decreased by 8–12ms for inference gateway; memory use marginally increased due to exporter buffers (configurable)
Follow-up tickets: ENG-7140 (metric-regression CI), ENG-7199 (collector autoscaler tuning)
